prompt: A data-analysis agent writes and runs Python code that you haven't reviewed.
tells: writes and runs Python code that you haven't reviewed
why: Execute it in an isolated container with no network or secrets and limited resources.
trap: Reviewing every snippet by hand defeats the point of the agent.

prompt: A support agent only needs to read orders, but it was given an admin API key that can also issue refunds and delete accounts.
why: Scope its credentials to exactly what it needs, so a mistake or injection can't do more.
trap: Approvals help, but the simpler fix is not granting the power at all.

prompt: A browsing agent reads untrusted web pages and also has access to the user's email. A malicious page could try to make it forward private emails.
tells: also has access to the user's email
why: Separate untrusted input from sensitive capabilities: isolate the browsing context and restrict what it can trigger.
trap: Approval prompts help, but limiting what the agent can reach is the stronger control.

prompt: A coding agent runs shell commands autonomously. You want any mistake limited to a throwaway copy of the repository.
why: Run it in an isolated workspace (container or worktree) so the blast radius is contained.
trap: Asking approval for every command makes autonomy pointless.
